messages:
alex_support: Customer report: SSE stream stops mid-response after switching from LTE -> WiFi on iOS 15. App sees partial JSON chunk and then connection closes. Customer quote: 'we get tokens of text then suddenly EOF, no error body'

marta_mobile: any client logs? app retry logic? which SDK version?

alex_support: iOS SDK 2.3.1, reproduction steps from customer: start streaming completion, then switch network, token refresh scheduled ~20s into the stream. They included a short log: 
```
[09:15:58] SSE open, headers ok (200)
[09:16:18] chunk: {"delta":"hello"}
[09:16:19] token refresh started
[09:16:20] socket closed (EOF)
```
No explicit 4xx in client logs.

sam_sre: Can you paste our ingress request_id / session id? If token rotates mid-stream client should re-open stream, but we should tolerate brief token handoffs. Also NAT timeouts/proxies can half-close sockets.

alex_support: Request_id: req-0a7f3c; session: sess-77. Customer says token was rotated by their auth server at ~09:16:19.

jenny_engineer: Looking at our edge traces for req-0a7f3c: we see a 401 to the upstream auth check at 2026-03-15T09:16:20. Followed by FIN from the edge to the client at 09:16:20. That matches their timing.

deploy-bot: CI deploy finished 2026-03-15T09:12:12Z, no auth changes in that deploy.

marta_mobile: I can reproduce locally on a device emulator. Repro steps I used: 
1) Start SSE stream against /v1/streams with Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>
2) After ~15s trigger server-side token rotation for that user
3) Switch network (cell -> wifi) during the token rotation window
Result: client receives partial JSON then the connection closes with no trailing error.

Commands I used to simulate SSE and token rotation: 
```bash
# open SSE in terminal (simple test)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate
# while stream running rotate token on auth server for that subject
```

jenny_engineer: Root cause hypothesis: token rotation triggers auth check failure at the edge while the long-lived TCP connection is mid-inflight, the edge then tears down the connection which leads to partial output on client. Network switch exacerbates because new path doesn't reuse the old socket; client sees EOF. Two contributing factors: short token TTL + auth rotation during streaming, and client not re-establishing/resuming the stream.

sam_sre: Short-term mitigation options: 
- Advise customer to keep a stream-specific session token until stream ends (pin token for stream lifetime).
- Implement client-side resume logic: open new SSE with resume token to fetch remainder.
- Server-side: add a 5s grace window where rotated tokens are accepted for existing connections (instrumentation first).

alex_support: I opened INC-4321 with the customer repro attached and asked them to try pinning the token as a workaround. Customer asked about billing for partial outputs — they want to be sure they aren't charged for truncated responses.

jenny_engineer: Billing note: server only counts fully committed tokens once response stream completes; partial chunks are currently counted as billed at production. Filing follow-up with billing: BILL-199 to evaluate prorating on aborted streams.

marta_mobile: Action items:
- @jenny_engineer add instrumentation to detect token-rotation-triggered closes for active SSE streams.
- @sam_sre investigate adding edge grace acceptance for rotated tokens and measure risk.
- alex_support: update customer with workaround and ETA.

alex_support: Updated customer and shared repro steps. They will test token pinning and report back. Thanks team :thumbsup:

sam_sre: I'll track infra side in INC-4321 and report whether a short-term edge tweak is safe to prototype.

jenny_engineer: If customer can't pin token we should prioritize server-side grace and a clear retry/resume pattern in SDK docs.

alex_support: Closing Slack thread for now, will re-open on updates to INC-4321.
